pass_b_english: …completely, easily, and very readily rejected. And indeed, God said, 'This people approaches me with their mouth and honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me; they worship me in vain, teaching the commandments of men' (Matthew 15:8-9). But our Lord Jesus Christ writes holy and divine laws for us on fleshy, that is, sensible, tablets of the heart. For He also spoke through the prophet Ezekiel, saying, 'I will remove their stony heart from their flesh and give them a fleshy heart, so that they may walk in my commandments' (Ezekiel 36:26). If someone, therefore, does not cling to the shadows through Moses, nor even have the law written in black on stone tablets, but rather has it in the mind through the Spirit, this is the letter of Christ known to all people.

What is the confidence we have through Christ towards God? Listen, then, to one approaching and saying: 'Not that we are sufficient from ourselves to think anything as from ourselves; for all wisdom is from the Lord' (1 Corinthians 4:2; James 1:17), as it is written: 'Every perfect gift is from above and from the Father of lights' (James 1:17). But the one through whom all things are, and in whom all things are, Christ, who mediates for us and for God through the economy, while working all things from God the Father, being both wisdom and power of His own being; what, then, is the confidence through Christ towards God? Listen, then, to one approaching and saying: 'Not that we are sufficient from ourselves to think anything as from ourselves; for all wisdom is from the Lord' (1 Corinthians 4:2), as it is written: 'For all wisdom is from the Lord' (James 1:17). But our sufficiency is from God, who has made us ministers of the new covenant, not of the letter but of the spirit; for the letter kills, but the spirit gives life. And what is the letter? In the law, it is a type, the things still being fulfilled in shadows; but the spirit is the power of the worship in Christ, declaring those approaching it through faith to be spiritual. As much as the type is inferior to the truth, so much, I think, are those serving it inferior to those performing the truth. For Christ sprinkles us with his own blood, and not only for the purity of the flesh, as also the things in the law, but rather he also cleanses our conscience from dead works and removes transgression; and he grants, in addition to this, the hope of life. For it is true that 'the one believing in the Son has eternal life' (John 3:36); for he has promised also the resurrection of their bodies and the restoration to incorruption and to a long life. For the glorified thing will not have been glorified in this part, because of the surpassing glory.

He refers again to the comparison of the axiom of the divine apostleship against the ministries, having made the comparison of the two and having brought forth their own, making more manifest the one in Christ through the spirit. And the scope of his thought comes through these things, but the statement is full yet not very clearly expressed; for it seems to be somehow not very easy to see, nor even ready for those who wish to see. What is the meaning of 'the glorified has not been glorified' and the following? There is something of this kind that he intends to make manifest. For Moses has been glorified, he says, as a minister of the law that is being abolished, but the glory of the new proclamation in Christ, overcoming the first, made it seem as if it had not been glorified at all. Just as when night is still present and the whole universe is grieving under its darkness, the circle of the moon flashes, but the chorus of the stars has its own glory …
